questions.question: According to the lecture, what best describes a thesis or dissertation?
options: A summary of all books read during the degree
A document submitted in support of candidature for a degree presenting original research and findings
A collection of random essays on a general topic
A biography of the author's professional life

questions.question: Regarding the terminology of 'Thesis' vs. 'Dissertation', which statement is true?
options: Thesis is always for a Doctorate and Dissertation for a Master's globally
There is no difference; they are exactly the same in every country
Usage varies by country; sometimes thesis is for a Master's and dissertation for a Doctorate, or vice versa
Dissertation is strictly for undergraduate studies only

questions.question: When defining the 'Research Problem' in a thesis, you should:
options: Focus only on what is already well-known
Avoid mentioning the background of the subject
Highlight the shortage in current knowledge to put the work in proper viewpoint
Keep the objectives vague and immeasurable

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT typically part of the General Structure of a thesis?
A good thesis title should be:
options: As long as possible to include every detail
Full of obscure abbreviations to sound technical
Vague so it appeals to everyone

questions.question: Who can ethically be listed as an author of a thesis?
options: An individual who made a significant intellectual contribution and approved the final version
A friend who proofread the grammar only

questions.question: What is the typical length limit for a thesis abstract mentioned in the lecture?
options: Typically not more than half to one page

questions.question: What should generally be avoided in an abstract?
The 'Body' of the thesis typically includes which sequence of chapters?
options: Introduction, Literature Review, Methodology, Findings, Analysis, Conclusion

questions.question: What is a key function of the Literature Review?
options: To pad the thesis with extra pages
To summarize the current state of knowledge and identify gaps
To list every book ever written on the topic
To copy existing theories without analysis

questions.question: The 'Materials & Method' section should include detailed information on:
options: Sampling technique, instrumentation specifications, and data analysis tools

questions.question: In the 'Discussion & Interpretation' chapter, the student must demonstrate:
options: Ability to recognize and deal with contradictions
Ability to ignore data that doesn't fit the hypothesis
Ability to repeat the results without analysis

questions.question: Which question is critical for the 'Final Analysis' of a thesis?
options: Did the thesis use a specific font size?
Has the thesis made a substantive original contribution to knowledge?

questions.question: Which of the following is listed as a characteristic of a 'Poor Thesis'?
An 'Outstanding Thesis' is characterized by:
options: Being an end in itself rather than opening new scenes

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT part of the structure of a research paper?
When writing a title for a research paper, you should:
options: Include abbreviations even if they are not commonly understood
Make it as general as possible
Include key phrases likely to be used in a search

questions.question: Regarding authorship ethics in a research paper:
options: You must include the department head even if they did nothing
You must not include any author if he/she has not made any contribution
You can include friends to help their careers

questions.question: What is the typical word count for a research paper abstract?
The primary goal of the research paper abstract is to:
options: Motivate people to read the paper
Explain the mathematical proofs in detail

questions.question: Which of the following should be included in the Introduction?
options: A repetition of the abstract word-for-word
The state of the general area of interest and the problem statement
The detailed code of the software used

questions.question: What is the purpose of the 'Related Work' section?
options: To give credit to previous work and establish the originality of the current work
To list unrelated papers to look smart

questions.question: Where can the 'Related Work' section be placed?
options: Either as part of the introduction or at the end of the body of the paper

questions.question: The 'Outline of the paper' typically appears:
options: At the end of the Introduction section

questions.question: For a Computer Science paper on applied research, the body structure typically includes:
options: Architecture of a new system, description, and evaluation
A biography of the computer inventor

questions.question: The 'Conclusion' section should:
options: Introduce new problems not mentioned before
Summarize the contribution and outline future directions

questions.question: Who should be thanked in the Acknowledgements?
options: External funding sources and non-authors who made significant contributions
People who did not read the paper

questions.question: What does 'Top down Design' mean in the context of writing hints?
options: Starting with an outline, then filling in the details
Writing from the bottom of the page up

questions.question: What is 'Inside out writing'?
options: Writing the body first, then introduction/conclusion, and finally the abstract
Writing the paper in a foreign language first
Writing the abstract, then the introduction, then the body

questions.question: When checking for 'Interpretability', you should:
options: Make sentences complex so they are hard to understand
Check whether each sentence could be misread and correct it if necessary
Use as many font colors as possible
